ca-foundation:
Who this pathway is for
Foundation is the starting route for students entering Chartered Accountancy. ICAI permits registration after Class 10; eligibility to sit the examination also depends on Class 12 and the prescribed study period. Check ICAI’s current conditions before selecting your attempt.

Plan your preparation
Build your accounting basics, practise numerical questions and set aside time for law and economics. Ask Logic admissions about the teaching plan, revision support and assessment arrangements for your chosen batch.

Before you enrol
Discuss your school schedule, target attempt and preferred campus or learning mode. Request the current fee details and confirm what is included in the batch.
ca-inter:
Choose your entry route
Intermediate can be entered after passing Foundation and Class 12, or through ICAI’s Direct Entry route for eligible candidates. Direct Entry includes commerce graduates/postgraduates with at least 55%, other graduates/postgraduates with at least 60%, and specified professional-examination routes. Confirm your individual eligibility and study-period requirements with ICAI.

Plan your preparation
Organise your study around the two groups, identify topics that need additional practice and allow time for revision and question-solving. Ask Logic about the teaching and assessment plan for the group or subjects you intend to take.

Choose a suitable batch
Share your previous exam progress, target attempt and available study hours. Admissions can help you check the current batch options, timetable and fees.
ca-final:
Your next professional stage
Final follows Intermediate in the CA pathway. Registration and examination eligibility are separate steps. Check ICAI’s current requirements for your training status, self-paced modules, advanced training and intended attempt, particularly if you converted from an older scheme.

Plan your preparation
Focus on connecting technical concepts with case-based application. Build a revision plan around your group or subject choices, practical-training commitments and areas that need more question practice.

Discuss your study options
Tell Logic admissions your target attempt and subject requirements. Ask about the relevant teaching plan, revision arrangements, available recorded classes and current fees before joining.
